description:
Morning Glory (Ipomoea spp.) is a climbing vine known for its bright, trumpet-shaped flowers. It is toxic to cats, with the biggest danger coming from the seeds.

The seeds contain ergine, a chemical compound that affects the brain and nervous system in a way similar to certain hallucinogens. The leaves and flowers also have toxins, but they mostly just bother the stomach.

If a cat eats the flowers or leaves, it may vomit or have diarrhea. However, eating the seeds can cause confusion, agitation, large pupils, and tremors. If you suspect your cat has eaten morning glory seeds or if they show unusual behavior, contact a veterinarian immediately.
name: Morning Glory
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: ergine (d-lysergic acid amide) and related indole alkaloids; concentrated in seeds
Mechanism: ergine acts on serotonin receptors in the CNS, causing altered neurological function; seeds also contain tannins that cause GI irritation
Symptoms: vomiting, diarrhea, drooling; seed ingestion may cause disorientation, agitation, dilated pupils, or tremors
Seeds are the most dangerous part; flowers and leaves cause mainly GI upset
Contact your vet if your cat ingests seeds or shows neurological symptoms
